verses.zh: 耶稣说完了这一切的话，就对门徒说：
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] Jesus had finished saying all these things, he told his disciples,
notes: Grk “And it happened when.” The introductory phrase καὶ ἐγένετο (kai egeneto, “it happened that”) is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 「你们知道，过两天是逾越节，人子将要被交给人，钉在十字架上。」
verses.en: “You know that after two days the Passover is coming, and the Son of Man will be handed over[NOTE:1] to be crucified.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “will be delivered up.”
See the note on crucified in 20:19.

verses.zh: 那时，祭司长和民间的长老聚集在大祭司称为该亚法的院里。
verses.en: Then the chief priests and the elders of the people met together in the palace of the high priest, who was named Caiaphas.

verses.zh: 大家商议要用诡计拿住耶稣，杀他，
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] planned to arrest Jesus by stealth and kill him.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 只是说：「当节的日子不可，恐怕民间生乱。」
verses.en: But they said, “Not during the feast, so that there won’t be a riot among the people.”[NOTE:1]
notes: The suggestion here is that Jesus was too popular to openly arrest him.

verses.zh: 耶稣在伯大尼长大麻疯的西门家里，
verses.en: Now while Jesus was in Bethany at the house of Simon the leper,[NOTE:1]
notes: See the note on leper in Matt 8:2.

verses.zh: 有一个女人拿着一玉瓶极贵的香膏来，趁耶稣坐席的时候，浇在他的头上。
verses.en: a woman came to him with an alabaster jar[NOTE:1] of expensive perfumed oil,[NOTE:2] and she poured it on his head as he was at the table.[NOTE:3]
notes: A jar made of alabaster stone was normally used for very precious substances like perfumes. It normally had a long neck which was sealed and had to be broken off so the contents could be used.

Mark specifies that the perfumed oil was Nard or spikenard, which is a fragrant oil from the root and spike of the nard plant of northern India (Mark 14:3). This perfumed oil, if made of something like nard, would have been extremely expensive, costing up to a year’s pay for an average laborer.tn Μύρον (muron) was usually made of myrrh (from which the English word is derived) but here it is used in the sense of ointment or perfumed oil (L&N 6.205).

Grk “as he was reclining.”sn 1st century middle eastern meals were not eaten while sitting at a table, but while reclining on one’s side on the floor with the head closest to the low table and the feet farthest away.

verses.zh: 门徒看见就很不喜悦，说：「何用这样的枉费呢！
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] the disciples saw this, they became indignant and said, “Why this waste?
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 这香膏可以卖许多钱，周济穷人。」
verses.en: It[NOTE:1] could have been sold at a high price and the money[NOTE:2] given to the poor!”
notes: Here γάρ (gar) has not been translated.
The words “the money” are not in the Greek text, but are implied (as the proceeds from the sale of the perfumed oil).

verses.zh: 耶稣看出他们的意思，就说：「为甚么难为这女人呢？她在我身上做的是一件美事。
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] Jesus learned of this, he said to them, “Why are you bothering this woman? She[NOTE:2] has done a good service for me.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
Grk “For she.” Here γάρ (gar) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 因为常有穷人和你们同在；只是你们不常有我。
verses.en: For you will always have the poor with you, but you will not always have me![NOTE:1]
notes: In the Greek text of this clause, “me” is in emphatic position (the first word in the clause). To convey some impression of the emphasis, an exclamation point is used in the translation.

verses.zh: 她将这香膏浇在我身上是为我安葬做的。
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] she poured this oil on my body, she did it to prepare me for burial.
notes: Grk “For when.” Here γάρ (gar) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 我实在告诉你们，普天之下，无论在甚么地方传这福音，也要述说这女人所行的，作个纪念。」
verses.en: I tell you the truth,[NOTE:1] wherever this gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”
notes: Grk “Truly (ἀμήν, amēn), I say to you.”

verses.zh: 当下，十二门徒里有一个称为加略人犹大的，去见祭司长，说：
verses.en: Then one of the twelve, the one named Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests

verses.zh: 「我把他交给你们，你们愿意给我多少钱？」他们就给了他三十块钱。
verses.en: and said, “What will you give me to betray him into your hands?”[NOTE:1] So they set out 30 silver coins for him.
notes: Grk “What will you give to me, and I will deliver him over to you?”

verses.zh: 从那时候，他就找机会要把耶稣交给他们。
verses.en: From that time[NOTE:1] on, Judas[NOTE:2] began looking for an opportunity to betray him.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.
Grk “he”; the referent (Judas) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 除酵节的第一天，门徒来问耶稣说：「你吃逾越节的筵席，要我们在哪里给你预备？」
verses.en: Now on the first day of the Feast of[NOTE:1] Unleavened Bread the disciples came to Jesus and said,[NOTE:2] “Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?”[NOTE:3]
notes: The words “the feast of” are not in the Greek text, but have been supplied for clarity.
Grk “the disciples came to Jesus, saying.” The participle λέγοντες (legontes) has been translated as a finite verb to make the sequence of events clear in English.

This required getting a suitable lamb and finding lodging in Jerusalem where the meal could be eaten. The population of the city swelled during the feast, so lodging could be difficult to find. The Passover was celebrated each year in commemoration of the Israelites’ deliverance from Egypt; thus it was a feast celebrating redemption (see Exod 12). The Passover lamb was roasted and eaten after sunset in a family group of at least ten people (m. Pesahim 7.13). People ate the meal while reclining (see the note on table in 26:20). It included, besides the lamb, unleavened bread and bitter herbs as a reminder of Israel’s bitter affliction at the hands of the Egyptians. Four cups of wine mixed with water were also used for the meal. For a further description of the meal and the significance of the wine cups, see E. Ferguson, Backgrounds of Early Christianity, 523-24.

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「你们进城去，到某人那里，对他说：『夫子说：我的时候快到了，我与门徒要在你家里守逾越节。』」
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] said, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, ‘The Teacher says, “My time is near. I will observe the Passover with my disciples at your house.”’”
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 门徒遵着耶稣所吩咐的就去预备了逾越节的筵席。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] the disciples did as Jesus had instructed them, and they prepared the Passover.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic.

verses.zh: 到了晚上，耶稣和十二个门徒坐席。
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] it was evening, he took his place at the table[NOTE:2] with the twelve.[NOTE:3]
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

Grk “he was reclining at table,” as 1st century middle eastern meals were not eaten while sitting at a table, but while reclining on one’s side on the floor with the head closest to the low table and the feet farthest away.

Many witnesses, some of them quite significant, have μαθητῶν (mathētōn, “disciples”; א A L W Δ Θ 33 892 1241 1424 pm lat) or μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ (mathētōn autou, “his disciples”; 0281 it) after δώδεκα (dōdeka, “twelve”). However, such clarifications are typical scribal expansions to the text. Further, the shorter reading (the one that ends with δώδεκα) has strong support in P37vid,45vid B D K Γ ƒ1,13 565 579 700 pm. Thus both internally and externally the reading that ends the verse with “the twelve” is to be preferred.

verses.zh: 正吃的时候，耶稣说：「我实在告诉你们，你们中间有一个人要卖我了。」
verses.en: And while they were eating he said, “I tell you the truth,[NOTE:1] one of you will betray me.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “Truly (ἀμήν, amēn), I say to you.”
Or “will hand me over.”

verses.zh: 他们就甚忧愁，一个一个地问他说：「主，是我吗？」
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] became greatly distressed[NOTE:2] and each one began to say to him, “Surely not I, Lord?”
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.
The participle λυπούμενοι (lupoumenoi) has been translated as a finite verb to make the sequence of events clear in English.

verses.zh: 耶稣回答说：「同我蘸手在盘子里的，就是他要卖我。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] answered, “The one who has dipped his hand into the bowl with me[NOTE:2] will betray me.
notes: Grk “answering, he said.” This is somewhat redundant and has been simplified in the translation. Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

The one who has dipped his hand into the bowl with me. The point of Jesus’ comment here is not to identify the specific individual per se, but to indicate that it is one who was close to him—somebody whom no one would suspect. His comment serves to heighten the treachery of Judas’ betrayal.

verses.zh: 人子必要去世，正如经上指着他所写的；但卖人子的人有祸了！那人不生在世上倒好。」
verses.en: The Son of Man will go as it is written about him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would be better for him if he had never been born.”

verses.zh: 卖耶稣的犹大问他说：「拉比，是我吗？」耶稣说：「你说的是。」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Judas, the one who would betray him, said, “Surely not I, Rabbi?” Jesus[NOTE:2] replied, “You have said it yourself.”
notes: Grk “answering, Judas.” This is somewhat redundant and has been simplified in the translation. Here δέ (de) has been translated as “then” to reflect the sequence of events in the narrative.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 他们吃的时候，耶稣拿起饼来，祝福，就擘开，递给门徒，说：「你们拿着吃，这是我的身体」；
verses.en: While[NOTE:1] they were eating, Jesus took bread, and after giving thanks he broke it, gave it to his disciples, and said, “Take, eat, this is my body.”
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 又拿起杯来，祝谢了，递给他们，说：「你们都喝这个；
verses.en: And after taking the cup and giving thanks, he gave it to them, saying, “Drink from it, all of you,

verses.zh: 因为这是我立约的血，为多人流出来，使罪得赦。
verses.en: for this is my blood, the blood[NOTE:1] of the covenant,[NOTE:2] that is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.
notes: Grk “for this is my blood of the covenant that is poured out for many.” In order to avoid confusion about which is poured out, the translation supplies “blood” twice so that the following phrase clearly modifies “blood,” not “covenant.”

Jesus’ death established the forgiveness promised in the new covenant of Jer 31:31. Jesus is reinterpreting the symbolism of the Passover meal, indicating the presence of a new era.tc Most witnesses, including several significant ones, read καινῆς (kainēs, “new”) here. Homoioteleuton is a possible reason for the omission, since the article, adjective, and noun are all first declension genitive singulars (τῆς καινῆς διαθήκης, tēs kainēs diathēkēs, “the new covenant”), but the likelihood of excellent, early, and sufficiently diverse witnesses all making the same mistake is remote. A much more probable scenario is that the addition of καινῆς was motivated by the parallel in Luke 22:20. It is a natural expansion on the text. Coupled with the fact that the shorter reading is found in such good and diverse witnesses (e.g., P37,45vid א B L Z Θ 0298vid 33 mae), it most likely is the initial text.

verses.zh: 但我告诉你们，从今以后，我不再喝这葡萄汁，直到我在我父的国里同你们喝新的那日子。」
verses.en: I[NOTE:1] tell you, from now on I will not drink of this fruit[NOTE:2] of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.”
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
Grk “produce” (“the produce of the vine” is a figurative expression for wine).

verses.zh: 他们唱了诗，就出来往橄榄山去。
verses.en: After[NOTE:1] singing a hymn,[NOTE:2] they went out to the Mount of Olives.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.

After singing a hymn. The Hallel Psalms (Pss 113-118) were sung during the meal. Psalms 113 and 114 were sung just before the second cup and 115-118 were sung at the end of the meal, after the fourth, or hallel cup.

verses.zh: 那时，耶稣对他们说：「今夜，你们为我的缘故都要跌倒。因为经上记着说：我要击打牧人，羊就分散了。
verses.en: Then Jesus said to them, “This night you will all fall away because of me, for it is written: “‘I will strike the shepherd,and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’[NOTE:1]
notes: A quotation from Zech 13:7.

verses.zh: 但我复活以后，要在你们以先往加利利去。」
verses.en: But after I am raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”

verses.zh: 彼得说：「众人虽然为你的缘故跌倒，我却永不跌倒。」
verses.en: Peter[NOTE:1] said to him, “If they all fall away because of you, I will never fall away!”
notes: Grk “answering, Peter said to him.” This is somewhat redundant and has been simplified in the translation. Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「我实在告诉你，今夜鸡叫以先，你要三次不认我。」
verses.en: Jesus said to him, “I tell you the truth,[NOTE:1] on this night, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”
notes: Grk “Truly (ἀμήν, amēn), I say to you.”

verses.zh: 彼得说：「我就是必须和你同死，也总不能不认你。」众门徒都是这样说。
verses.en: Peter said to him, “Even if I must die with you, I will never deny you.” And all the disciples said the same thing.

verses.zh: 耶稣同门徒来到一个地方，名叫客西马尼，就对他们说：「你们坐在这里，等我到那边去祷告。」
verses.en: Then Jesus went with them to a place called Gethsemane, and he said to the disciples, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”

verses.zh: 于是带着彼得和西庇太的两个儿子同去，就忧愁起来，极其难过，
verses.en: He took with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and he became anguished and distressed.

verses.zh: 便对他们说：「我心里甚是忧伤，几乎要死；你们在这里等候，和我一同警醒。」
verses.en: Then he said to them, “My soul is deeply grieved, even to the point of death. Remain here and stay awake with me.”

verses.zh: 他就稍往前走，俯伏在地，祷告说：「我父啊，倘若可行，求你叫这杯离开我。然而，不要照我的意思，只要照你的意思。」
verses.en: Going a little farther, he threw himself down with his face to the ground and prayed,[NOTE:1] “My Father, if possible,[NOTE:2] let this cup[NOTE:3] pass from me! Yet not what I will, but what you will.”
notes: Grk “ground, praying and saying.” Here the participle λέγων (legōn) is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.
Grk “if it is possible.”
This cup alludes to the wrath of God that Jesus would experience (in the form of suffering and death) for us. See Pss 11:6; 75:8-9; Isa 51:17, 19, 22 for this figure.

verses.zh: 来到门徒那里，见他们睡着了，就对彼得说：「怎么样？你们不能同我警醒片时吗？
verses.en: Then he came to the disciples and found them sleeping. He[NOTE:1] said to Peter, “So, couldn’t you stay awake with me for one hour?
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 总要警醒祷告，免得入了迷惑。你们心灵固然愿意，肉体却软弱了。」
verses.en: Stay awake and pray that you will not fall into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.”

verses.zh: 第二次又去祷告说：「我父啊，这杯若不能离开我，必要我喝，就愿你的意旨成全。」
verses.en: He went away a second time and prayed,[NOTE:1] “My Father, if this cup[NOTE:2] cannot be taken away unless I drink it, your will must be done.”
notes: Grk “saying.” The participle λέγων (legōn) is redundant here in contemporary English and has not been translated.
Grk “this”; the referent (the cup) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 又来，见他们睡着了，因为他们的眼睛困倦。
verses.en: He came again and found them sleeping; they could not keep their eyes open.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “because their eyes were weighed down,” an idiom for becoming extremely or excessively sleepy (L&N 23.69).

verses.zh: 耶稣又离开他们去了。第三次祷告，说的话还是与先前一样。
verses.en: So leaving them again, he went away and prayed for the third time, saying the same thing once more.

verses.zh: 于是来到门徒那里，对他们说：「现在你们仍然睡觉安歇吧（吧：或译吗？）！时候到了，人子被卖在罪人手里了。
verses.en: Then he came to the disciples and said to them, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the hour is approaching, and the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

verses.zh: 起来！我们走吧。看哪，卖我的人近了。」
verses.en: Get up, let us go. Look! My betrayer[NOTE:1] is approaching!”
notes: Grk “the one who betrays me.”

verses.zh: 说话之间，那十二个门徒里的犹大来了，并有许多人带着刀棒，从祭司长和民间的长老那里与他同来。
verses.en: While he was still speaking, Judas,[NOTE:1] one of the twelve, arrived. With him was a large crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and elders of the people.
notes: Grk “behold, Judas.” The Greek word ἰδού (idou) has not been translated because it has no exact English equivalent here, but adds interest and emphasis (BDAG 468 s.v. 1).

verses.zh: 那卖耶稣的给了他们一个暗号，说：「我与谁亲嘴，谁就是他。你们可以拿住他。」
verses.en: (Now the betrayer[NOTE:1] had given them a sign, saying, “The one I kiss is the man.[NOTE:2] Arrest him!”)[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “the one who betrays him.”
Grk “The one I kiss is he.”
This remark is parenthetical within the narrative and has thus been placed in parentheses.

verses.zh: 犹大随即到耶稣跟前，说：「请拉比安」，就与他亲嘴。
verses.en: Immediately[NOTE:1] he went up to Jesus and said, “Greetings, Rabbi,” and kissed him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.
Judas’ act of betrayal when he kissed Jesus is especially sinister when it is realized that it was common in the culture of the times for a disciple to kiss his master when greeting him.

verses.zh: 耶稣对他说：「朋友，你来要做的事，就做吧。」于是那些人上前，下手拿住耶稣。
verses.en: Jesus[NOTE:1] said to him, “Friend, do what you are here to do.” Then they came and took hold[NOTE:2] of Jesus and arrested him.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
Grk “and put their hands on Jesus.”

verses.zh: 有跟随耶稣的一个人伸手拔出刀来，将大祭司的仆人砍了一刀，削掉了他一个耳朵。
verses.en: But[NOTE:1] one of those with Jesus grabbed[NOTE:2] his sword, drew it out, and struck the high priest’s slave,[NOTE:3] cutting off his ear.
notes: Grk “And behold one.” The Greek word ἰδού (idou) has not been translated because it has no exact English equivalent here, but adds interest and emphasis (BDAG 468 s.v. 1).
Grk “extending his hand, drew out his sword, and struck.” Because rapid motion is implied in the circumstances, the translation “grabbed” was used.
See the note on the word “slave” in 8:9.

verses.zh: 耶稣对他说：「收刀入鞘吧！凡动刀的，必死在刀下。
verses.en: Then Jesus said to him, “Put your sword back in its place![NOTE:1] For all who take hold of the sword will die by the sword.
notes: The translation “put your sword back in its place” for this phrase is given in L&N 85.52.

verses.zh: 你想，我不能求我父现在为我差遣十二营多天使来吗？
verses.en: Or do you think that I cannot call on my Father and that he would send me more than 12 legions[NOTE:1] of angels right now?
notes: A legion was a Roman army unit of about 6,000 soldiers, so 12 legions would be 72,000.

verses.zh: 若是这样，经上所说，事情必须如此的话怎么应验呢？」
verses.en: How then would the scriptures that say it must happen this way be fulfilled?”

verses.zh: 当时，耶稣对众人说：「你们带着刀棒出来拿我，如同拿强盗吗？我天天坐在殿里教训人，你们并没有拿我。
verses.en: At that moment Jesus said to the crowd, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest me like you would an outlaw?[NOTE:1] Day after day I sat teaching in the temple courts, yet[NOTE:2] you did not arrest me.
notes: Or “a revolutionary.” This term can refer to one who stirs up rebellion: BDAG 594 s.v. λῃστής 2 has “revolutionary, insurrectionist, guerrilla” citing evidence from Josephus (J. W. 2.13.2-3 [2.253-254]). However, this usage generally postdates Jesus’ time. It does refer to a figure of violence. Luke uses the same term for the highwaymen who attack the traveler in the parable of the good Samaritan (Luke 10:30).
Grk “and” (καί, kai), a conjunction that is elastic enough to be used to indicate a contrast, as here.

verses.zh: 但这一切的事成就了，为要应验先知书上的话。」当下，门徒都离开他逃走了。
verses.en: But this has happened so that the scriptures of the prophets would be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples left him and fled.

verses.zh: 拿耶稣的人把他带到大祭司该亚法那里去；文士和长老已经在那里聚会。
verses.en: Now the ones who had arrested Jesus led him to Caiaphas, the high priest, in whose house[NOTE:1] the experts in the law[NOTE:2] and the elders had gathered.
notes: Grk “where.”
Or “where the scribes.” See the note on the phrase “experts in the law” in 2:4.

verses.zh: 彼得远远地跟着耶稣，直到大祭司的院子，进到里面，就和差役同坐，要看这事到底怎样。
verses.en: But Peter was following him from a distance, all the way to the high priest’s courtyard. After[NOTE:1] going in, he sat with the guards[NOTE:2] to see the outcome.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.
The guards would have been the guards of the chief priests who had accompanied Judas to arrest Jesus.

verses.zh: 祭司长和全公会寻找假见证控告耶稣，要治死他。
verses.en: The[NOTE:1] chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were trying to find false testimony against Jesus so that they could put him to death.
notes: Grk “Now the.” Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 虽有好些人来作假见证，总得不着实据。末后有两个人前来，说：
verses.en: But they did not find anything, though many false witnesses came forward. Finally[NOTE:1] two came forward
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 「这个人曾说：『我能拆毁　神的殿，三日内又建造起来。』」
verses.en: and declared, “This man[NOTE:1] said, ‘I am able to destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days.’”
notes: Grk “This one.”

verses.zh: 大祭司就站起来，对耶稣说：「你甚么都不回答吗？这些人作见证告你的是甚么呢？」
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] the high priest stood up and said to him, “Have you no answer? What is this that they are testifying against you?”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of the false testimony.

verses.zh: 耶稣却不言语。大祭司对他说：「我指着永生　神叫你起誓告诉我们，你是　神的儿子基督不是？」
verses.en: But Jesus was silent. The[NOTE:1] high priest said to him, “I charge you under oath by the living God, tell us if you are the Christ,[NOTE:2] the Son of God.”
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.
Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”sn See the note on Christ in 1:16.

verses.zh: 耶稣对他说：「你说的是。然而，我告诉你们，后来你们要看见人子坐在那权能者的右边，驾着天上的云降临。」
verses.en: Jesus said to him, “You have said it yourself. But I tell you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand[NOTE:1] of the Power[NOTE:2] and coming on the clouds of heaven.”[NOTE:3]
notes: An allusion to Ps 110:1. This is a claim that Jesus shares authority with God in heaven. Those present may have thought they were his judges, but, in fact, the reverse was true.
The expression the Power is a circumlocution for referring to God. Such indirect references to God were common in 1st century Judaism out of reverence for the divine name.
An allusion to Dan 7:13 (see also Matt 24:30).

verses.zh: 大祭司就撕开衣服，说：「他说了僭妄的话，我们何必再用见证人呢？这僭妄的话，现在你们都听见了。
verses.en: Then the high priest tore his clothes and declared,[NOTE:1] “He has blasphemed! Why do we still need witnesses? Now[NOTE:2] you have heard the blasphemy!
notes: Grk “the high priest tore his clothes, saying.”
Grk “Behold now.” The Greek word ἰδού (idou) has not been translated because it has no exact English equivalent here, but adds interest and emphasis (BDAG 468 s.v. 1).

verses.zh: 你们的意见如何？」他们回答说：「他是该死的。」
verses.en: What is your verdict?”[NOTE:1] They[NOTE:2] answered, “He is guilty and deserves[NOTE:3] death.”
notes: Grk “What do you think?”
Grk “answering, they said.” This is somewhat redundant and has been simplified in the translation. Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

Grk “he is guilty of death.” L&N 88.313 states, “pertaining to being guilty and thus deserving some particular penalty—‘guilty and deserving, guilty and punishable by.’ οἱ δὲ ἀποκριθέντες εἶπαν, ᾿Ενοχος θανάτου ἐστίν ‘they answered, He is guilty and deserves death’ Mt 26:66.”

verses.zh: 他们就吐唾沫在他脸上，用拳头打他；也有用手掌打他的，说：
verses.en: Then they spat in his face and struck him with their fists. And some slapped him,

verses.zh: 「基督啊！你是先知，告诉我们打你的是谁？」
verses.en: saying, “Prophesy for us, you Christ![NOTE:1] Who hit you?”[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”sn See the note on Christ in 1:16.
Grk “Who is the one who hit you?”sn Who hit you? This is a variation of one of three ancient games that involved blindfolds.

verses.zh: 彼得在外面院子里坐着，有一个使女前来，说：「你素来也是同那加利利人耶稣一伙的。」
verses.en: Now Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. A[NOTE:1] slave girl[NOTE:2] came to him and said, “You also were with Jesus the Galilean.”
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.
The Greek term here is παιδίσκη (paidiskē), referring to a slave girl or slave woman.

verses.zh: 彼得在众人面前却不承认，说：「我不知道你说的是甚么！」
verses.en: But he denied it in front of them all:[NOTE:1] “I don’t know what you’re talking about!”
notes: Grk “he denied it…saying.” The participle λέγων (legōn) is redundant in English and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 既出去，到了门口，又有一个使女看见他，就对那里的人说：「这个人也是同拿撒勒人耶稣一伙的。」
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] he went out to the gateway, another slave girl[NOTE:2] saw him and said to the people there, “This man was with Jesus the Nazarene.”
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
The words “slave girl” are not in the Greek text, but are implied by the feminine singular form ἄλλη (allē).

verses.zh: 彼得又不承认，并且起誓说：「我不认得那个人。」
verses.en: He denied it again with an oath, “I do not know the man!”

verses.zh: 过了不多的时候，旁边站着的人前来，对彼得说：「你真是他们一党的，你的口音把你露出来了。」
verses.en: After[NOTE:1] a little while, those standing there came up to Peter and said, “You really are one of them too—even your accent[NOTE:2] gives you away!”
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
Grk “your speech.”

verses.zh: 彼得就发咒起誓地说：「我不认得那个人。」立时，鸡就叫了。
verses.en: At that he began to curse, and he swore with an oath, “I do not know the man!” At that moment a rooster crowed.[NOTE:1]
notes: It seems most likely that this refers to a real rooster crowing, although a number of scholars have suggested that “cockcrow” is a technical term referring to the trumpet call which ended the third watch of the night (from midnight to 3 a.m.). This would then be a reference to the Roman gallicinium (ἀλεκτοροφωνία, alektorophōnia; the term is used in Mark 13:35 and is found in some mss [P37vid,45 ƒ1] in Matt 26:34) which would have been sounded at 3 a.m.; in this case Jesus would have prophesied a precise time by which the denials would have taken place. For more details see J. H. Bernard, St. John (ICC), 2:604. However, in light of the fact that Mark mentions the rooster crowing twice (Mark 14:72) and in Luke 22:60 the words are reversed (ἐφώνησεν ἀλέκτωρ, ephōnēsen alektōr), it is more probable that a real rooster is in view. In any event natural cockcrow would have occurred at approximately 3 a.m. in Palestine at this time of year (March-April) anyway.

verses.zh: 彼得想起耶稣所说的话：「鸡叫以先，你要三次不认我。」他就出去痛哭。
verses.en: Then Peter remembered what Jesus had said: “Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.” And he went outside and wept bitterly.[NOTE:1]
notes: When Peter went out and wept bitterly it shows he really did not want to fail here and was deeply grieved that he had.
